system: civil law system with influences from Argentine, Spanish, Roman, and French civil law models; Supreme Court of Justice reviews legislative acts

constitution.history: several previous; latest approved and promulgated 20 June 1992
constitution.amend: proposed at the initiative of at least one quarter of either chamber of the National Congress, by the president of the republic, or by petition of at least 30,000 voters; passage requires a two-thirds majority vote by both chambers and approval in a referendum

courts.highest: Supreme Court of Justice or Corte Suprema de Justicia (consists of 9 justices divided 3 each into the Constitutional Court, Civil and Commercial Chamber, and Criminal Division)
courts.judges: justices proposed by the Council of Magistrates or Consejo de la Magistratura, a 6-member independent body, and appointed by the Chamber of Senators with presidential concurrence; judges can serve until mandatory retirement at age 75
courts.lower: appellate courts; first instance courts; minor courts, including justices of the peace

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a native-born citizen of Paraguay

suffrage: 18 years of age; universal and compulsory until the age of 75
world: accepts compulsory ICJ jurisdiction; accepts ICCt jurisdiction
